subject.title: Bound historical public repository proof reuse after expiry

question: Should outage fallback allow the proposed five-second grace after a public-repository proof expires, or should it fail closed immediately?
rationale: The acceptable post-expiry authorization window is a security-policy choice; implementation can make either policy consistent, but should not choose the trust boundary without maintainer approval.

options.title: Approve a five-second grace
options.body: Land the linked repair with a five-second maximum post-expiry window enforced identically by runtime and D1 validation.

options.title: Fail closed at expiry
options.body: Require historical proofs to remain unexpired and revise the linked repair and tests to remove post-expiry reuse.

recommendation.title: Approve a five-second grace
recommendation.body: Land the linked repair with a five-second maximum post-expiry window enforced identically by runtime and D1 validation.

likelyOwner.reason: The available merged history ties steipete most directly to the existing public-proof fallback behavior.
